breaking.headline: Schumer accuses Nvidia CEO Huang of violating export controls
breaking.fact: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Tuesday that Jensen Huang 'shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law,' likening it to selling rocket engines to the Soviets in the Space Race. Schumer urged quick passage of bipartisan chip-export bills; Huang is set to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

breaking.headline: Iraq presses OPEC+ for a higher output capacity estimate
breaking.fact: Baghdad is challenging an OPEC+ review that puts its maximum sustainable output below 5 million barrels a day, pressing for a baseline near 6 million ahead of the group's Nov. 29 meeting on 2027 quotas. The IEA puts Iraq's sustainable capacity at 4.87 million; Iraq says it already pumps more than 5 million.

breaking.headline: U.S. home price growth held steady in September
breaking.fact: U.S. home price growth continued its steady climb in September, once again led by major cities including Chicago and New York, according to Dow Jones. The steady gains keep housing affordability tight heading into year-end.

breaking.headline: German business sentiment rises again in November
breaking.fact: Business sentiment in Europe's largest economy improved again in November, with firms reporting brighter conditions and expectations, reflecting the enduring recovery from years of subdued growth. The reading adds to signs Europe's industrial slump is easing.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide edged up in Paris to €188.12, worth $206.24 at the ECB's Nov 24 reference rate of 1.0963, a 0.5% dollar gain on the day. The industrial-gas giant is quietly outperforming while U.S. tech gives back Monday's rally, its defensive profile doing the work. The euro sparkline shows a slow, orderly drift. With no company news in play, the dollar price from here mostly tracks the euro's moves.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic fell 9.3% to $79.47 on Tuesday, sliding further below its $83 IPO price a week after listing as the AI trade unwound. The stock has given back its entire debut pop, with chips and memory names leading the retreat after Monday's record rally. With the listing barely a week old, the tape is still finding its level. Watch whether $83 flips from support to resistance now that the stock trades beneath it.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up 0.02% to $91.62, its usual slow grind as the Treasury bill ETF accrues interest. The fund keeps paying its monthly distribution — $0.30849 per share, ex Nov 2, paid Nov 5 — and the distribution yield sits at 4.04%. It is the quiet corner of the watchlist: no drama, just steady Treasury income. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, short rates stay the story here.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet slipped 1.8% to $277.08 as Tuesday's tariff headlines and the AI unwind dragged tech lower after Monday's 4.7% S&P surge. The pullback is broad rather than Alphabet-specific, with the Nasdaq down nearly 2% while the Dow holds up on defensive rotation. Google's AI and cloud story is unchanged by a day's tape. Watch whether buyers step in near Monday's breakout levels or the rally fades further.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly jumped 3.5% to $1,412.81, one of Tuesday's few big gainers, after Moody's upgraded the drugmaker to Aa2 (stable). The agency cited the massive growth potential of incretin therapies Mounjaro and Zepbound, the engine of Lilly's recent run. Healthcare led the tape as investors rotated out of chips and into defensives. The upgrade is a fresh fundamental stamp on a stock already priced for strong growth.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere inched up 0.1% to $295.86, holding near its highs while the broader market pulled back on tariff worries. Natural gas and LNG names are caught between firm energy prices — WTI crude is up about 2% today — and a risk-off tape punishing growth. Cheniere's contracted export volumes keep its cash flows steady through the noise. Watch gas prices and any fresh export headlines for the next move.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia slid 7.6% to $152.51, giving back part of Monday's 31.5% surge on Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Tuesday brought fresh pressure: Senate leader Schumer accused Huang of violating chip-export law, and new tariff headlines hit chips. The stock remains far above pre-reinstatement levels, but the probes and Dec 1 testimony still hang over it. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes shake out.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer climbed 4.1% to $28.53, riding Tuesday's defensive rotation as healthcare led the tape while tech slid. Pharma names are catching a bid with investors seeking shelter from the AI unwind and tariff headlines. The move adds to a steady recent run for a stock Sean holds for income as much as growth. Watch whether the sector rotation holds into the Thanksgiving-shortened week.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab dropped 6.9% to $46.23 as growth and space names sold off with the Nasdaq's near-2% slide. The pullback is tape-driven rather than company-specific — no fresh Rocket Lab news today — after a strong run that left the stock sensitive to risk-off days. The company remains a core speculative holding with a busy manifest ahead. Watch whether a steadier tape turns this dip into a buying chance.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 5.0% to $8.57, one of the day's strongest watchlist names as investors rotated toward yield and defensives. Mortgage REITs are catching a bid with the 10-year Treasury yield steady near 4.91% and rate-cut hopes still alive for December. The move extends a solid stretch for a high-dividend holding. Watch the Fed's December meeting for the next read on the rate path.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX, the leveraged Nasdaq ETF, fell 5.6% to $125.90 as the Nasdaq slid nearly 2% on the AI unwind and tariff headlines. Leveraged funds magnify the tape in both directions, so a day like this cuts both ways — Monday's surge was equally outsized. The position is a trading vehicle, not a buy-and-hold, and days like today are the cost of the leverage. Watch whether tech stabilizes after Thanksgiving.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist edged up 0.8% to $47.28, holding its ground while the broader market pulled back. Banks are benefiting from the defensive rotation and a steady 10-year yield near 4.91%, with regional lenders quietly outperforming growth names. Truist's dividend and steady earnings keep it a workhorse holding. Watch the Fed's December decision and any fresh tariff news for the next direction.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony fell 7.3% to $2.22, giving back part of Monday's bounce as the small-cap tape sold off. The stock had fired the bottom-watch tripwire at Friday's close, and the Nov 23 rebound carried it to $2.39 before today's pullback. China's suspension of some critical-material export curbs until January keeps the supply-squeeze thesis on hold. The watch resumes at 8:18 AM CT for the next bottom signal.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy slid 3.8% to $5.62, easing after Monday's 10% surge off Friday's $5.30 low that re-armed the bottom watch. The pullback is broad — small caps and growth are selling off on tariff headlines — rather than uranium-specific. Nuclear expansion and government uranium buying remain the longer-term catalysts Sean is watching. The daily gap watch resumes at 8:18 AM CT for any 5-point-plus move.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 1.3% to $325.17 while WTI crude rose about 2% to $81.76, refiners lagging the energy rally on a risk-off day. The stock is a locked work-related holding, so the day-to-day tape matters less than the refining margin picture. Gulf Coast refining cracks stay the fundamental driver here. Watch OPEC+'s Nov 29 meeting on 2027 quotas for the next oil-price signal.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund still shows its $28.51 NAV from Nov 23, unchanged until tonight's pricing — mutual funds strike NAV once a day after the close. The diversified mix of stocks and bonds smooths days like Tuesday, when the Nasdaq slid nearly 2% while the Dow rose. It is the set-and-forget anchor of the watchlist, rebalancing as retirement approaches. Watch for Tuesday's NAV tomorrow.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate puts VI5TC at $147.56, down 0.8% with Tuesday's market pullback after Monday's rally. The estimator tracks the S&P 500's move from its Nov 3 anchor, and Sean's own check put it within about 0.1% of the real price. The fund's actual holdings are index-linked, so the estimate moves tick-for-tick with the market. A steadier tape should lift the estimate back toward $149.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund still sits at its $1.00 NAV, paying a 7-day SEC yield of 3.78% as published Nov 23 by Schwab. The wind-down continues: balances over $1,000 keep moving into CDs under the November plan, so the position should keep shrinking. The inherited-IRA slice is exempt from the nudge until March. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, money-fund yields may edge up rather than down.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03%, published Nov 23 by Vanguard. It remains the top-yielding cash on the watchlist and the parking spot for the ANT proceeds and the Seiver Slough and Lodge sale streams in the income model. The fund owns only Treasuries, so it carries no credit risk. A December Fed hike would likely lift its yield further.

weekInBrief.headline: Bank of Canada signals a December rate hike may be coming
weekInBrief.body: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem warned Tuesday that persistent inflation driven by oil shocks and supply disruptions could require further rate hikes, with market-implied odds for a December increase jumping to 80%. He also said year-end inflation may come in below the 3.5% forecast issued in October as crude prices and refinery margins retreat.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed revises industrial production data; factory capacity growth slows
weekInBrief.body: The Federal Reserve's revised data show manufacturing output rose more than 3.25% from December 2022 through October 2026, but capacity growth was revised down by half a point to about 0.5% a year after 2022. October manufacturing capacity utilization reached 77.1%.

weekInBrief.headline: Moody's lifts Eli Lilly to Aa2 on weight-loss drug growth
weekInBrief.body: Moody's upgraded Eli Lilly to Aa2 with a stable outlook, citing the massive growth potential of its incretin therapies Mounjaro and Zepbound. The upgrade lands as Lilly shares climb about 3.5% Tuesday, one of the day's few big gainers as tech slides.

weekInBrief.headline: Singapore's economy is on track for its best year since 2011
weekInBrief.body: Singapore delivered a third straight quarter of above-6% growth, putting the economy on course for its strongest year since 2011 outside the post-pandemic rebound, powered by the AI boom. The city-state's run shows how the AI buildout is lifting Asia's trade-linked economies.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran's army chief, Gen. Amir Hatami, called Tuesday for tightening the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, while the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported two tankers struck by unknown projectiles near Khasab, Oman, on Saturday. President Trump said Sunday that Iran launched more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, all of them downed with no damage, and the Treasury Department on Friday sanctioned four Iranians it called “oil trustees” for moving illicit oil revenue. Iranian crude exports remain near zero since the blockade was restored on July 14 — TankerTrackers says one tanker loaded Iranian crude by ship-to-ship transfer last week, though Tehran dismissed the report as speculation — while Gulf oil keeps flowing through the strait, with about 4.18 million barrels aboard ships that crossed in the past 24 hours, per AIS tracking, virtually all of it non-Iranian.

space.headline: Hubble's new view of barred spiral NGC 4394
space.body: The Hubble Space Telescope released a fresh portrait of NGC 4394, a barred spiral galaxy about 55 million light-years away in the Virgo Cluster that closely resembles what the Milky Way would look like face-on. Its straight central bar of stars stands out among graceful spiral arms; astronomers estimate 65% of nearby spirals have bars, though how they form is still debated. The image folds in recent observations studying how star formation ends in crowded cluster galaxies.

space.headline: Dark Energy Camera captures the Betta Fish Nebula in finest detail yet
space.body: NSF NOIRLab released the sharpest view yet of supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7, nicknamed the Betta Fish Nebula for its wispy blue ribbons resembling the tropical fish’s flowing tails. The 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter telescope in Chile caught the remnant, some 6,800 light-years away in Centaurus, with a neutron star sitting inside its glowing shell. It may be the first professional-observatory image of this nebula.

space.headline: A Neanderthal gene variant may guard against schizophrenia
space.body: A Neanderthal variant near the DAAM1 gene is linked to slightly smaller occipital lobes in modern humans — about 0.85 cubic cm, roughly a blueberry’s volume — yet carriers showed no intelligence penalty, researchers led by Svante Pääbo and Hugo Zeberg report in a study published today. Carriers had a 5% lower risk of schizophrenia with one copy and nearly 10% lower with two, and scored higher on extraversion.

space.headline: Wernicke's area does double duty in speech, rewriting a 150-year-old map
space.body: A study in Science finds Wernicke’s area — long thought to handle only speech comprehension — also helps produce speech, upending the textbook split with Broca’s area. In 28 epilepsy-surgery patients with electrode grids, neurons in a small part of Wernicke’s area fired about a quarter-second before they spoke, more strongly for longer words like “caterpillar” than “cat.” The result could shape brain-computer interfaces that restore speech.

apod.title: Martian Dawn
apod.explanation: NASA's Curiosity rover captures dawn breaking over wind-carved cliffs on Mars in this close-up from a panorama released Oct. 6, 2026 — the most detailed view yet of distant yardangs, elongated ridges sculpted by wind erosion. The panorama was taken by Curiosity's Mastcam on Aug. 11, its 4,982nd Martian day, and stitches together six images.
